findings.finding: There is no opening review of checking equal side ratios or identifying the hypotenuse, although the introductory SSS, SAS and RHS illustrations depend directly on these skills.
findings.breakdown: Students must compare corresponding side ratios and distinguish the hypotenuse from a leg to interpret the tests. Neither skill is rehearsed before the illustrations and identification questions.
findings.checked: Checked all supplied teaching and practice; teachingComplete is true and there is no preceding topic or review. Retained ratio checks and hypotenuse recognition. Removed triangle angle sum: the AAA definition explicitly supplies the third-angle conclusion, and no introductory example requires calculating a third angle.
findings.assumptions: Ratio comparison and hypotenuse recognition are prior knowledge. Teacher-led review can reveal recall gaps. These items require no calculator.

repair.proposal: Before p3-tests, add: (1) Calculate 8/4, 12/6 and 14/7. Are all three ratios equal? (2) Calculate 9/3 and 8/2. Are the ratios equal? (3) Triangle ABC has a right angle at B. Name its hypotenuse. (4) Triangle PQR has a right angle at Q. Name its hypotenuse. Answers: (1) 2, 2, 2; yes. (2) 3 and 4; no. (3) AC. (4) PR. These four short items fit comfortably within a one-page review.

findings.doneWhen: Students rehearse equal-ratio checks and hypotenuse recognition before using the four similarity tests.

findings.finding: Extend the final altitude construction to explain the similarity of all three triangles and derive a relationship between the altitude and the hypotenuse segments.
findings.breakdown: This returns to the common-angle and right-angle reasoning in p10-q14-a, then applies corresponding-side ratios as in p10-q14-b.
findings.checked: For a nondegenerate right triangle, the altitude meets the hypotenuse internally. The ordered correspondences ABC ∼ ACD ∼ CBD are correct. Comparing the smaller triangles gives AD/CD = CD/DB, hence CD² = AD×DB. The task requires no new similarity test or geometric theorem.
findings.assumptions: All triangles are nondegenerate and all segment lengths are positive. Students use the corresponding-side ratio method already required by the final question.

repair.proposal: After p10-q14-b, offer this optional extension: In right triangle ABC, angle C is 90°. D lies on hypotenuse AB and CD is perpendicular to AB. Prove that triangles ABC, ACD and CBD are all similar. Then show that CD² = AD×DB. Expected answer: ABC ∼ ACD by the common angle at A and equal right angles; ABC ∼ CBD by the common angle at B and equal right angles. Thus ACD ∼ CBD. Corresponding sides give AD/CD = CD/DB, so CD² = AD×DB.

findings.doneWhen: The optional task includes the correct vertex correspondences and the expected ratio argument.
